rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening can mean the conquest of Mecca.
rows.anchor: أحدها : فتح مكة وهو ظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is the conquest of the Romans and other lands.
rows.anchor: وثانيها : فتح الروم وغيرها وثالثها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation identifies the opening with the treaty of al-Hudaybiyya.
rows.anchor: المراد من الفتح صلح الحديبية ورابعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is Islam's triumph through proof and argument, as well as sword and spear.
rows.anchor: ورابعها : فتح الإسلام بالحجة والبرهان ، والسيف والسنان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes fatḥ as judgment, as in the prayers for God to judge between peoples.
rows.anchor: المراد منه الحكم كقوله { ربنا افتح بيننا وبين قومنا بالحق }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi prefers Mecca, al-Hudaybiyya, and Islam's victory through signs, explanation, proof, and argument.
rows.anchor: والمختار من الكل وجوه : أحدها : فتح مكة ، والثاني : فتح الحديبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mecca reading fits 47:38: after urging spending, God says the conquest yielded homes and far more than believers spent, so withholding harmed only them.
rows.anchor: بين تعالى أنه فتح لهم مكة وغنموا ديارهم وحصل لهم أضعاف ما أنفقوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conquest demonstrates God's promise that the believers would be superior.
rows.anchor: بين برهانه بفتح مكة ، فإنهم كانوا هم الأعلون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command not to initiate peace means to persevere until opponents seek it; al-Hudaybiyya and Mecca exemplify this, when Quraysh leaders came seeking safety, faith, and submission.
rows.anchor: لا تسألوا الصلح من عندكم ، بل اصبروا فإنهم يسألون الصلح ويجتهدون فيه كما كان يوم الحديبية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the verse means Mecca before its conquest, one answer is that God speaks of the opening as already decreed.
rows.anchor: فتحنا في حكمنا وتقديرنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second answer is that God's decree is certain to occur, so the past tense signals an event none can prevent or reverse.
rows.anchor: ما قدره الله تعالى فهو كائن ، فأخبر بصيغة الماضي إشارة إلى أنه أمر لا دافع له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer says the opening causes the whole set of promised benefits, not forgiveness alone: completed favor, guidance, and victory as well.
rows.anchor: الفتح لم يجعله سببا للمغفرة وحدها ، بل هو سبب لاجتماع الأمور المذكورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mecca's conquest purified God's House of idols, and purification of the House became purification of His servant.
rows.anchor: فتح مكة كان سببا لتطهير بيت الله تعالى من رجس الأوثان ، وتطهير بيته صار سببا لتطهير عبده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conquest enables pilgrimage, which brings forgiveness; Razi cites the Prophet's prayer for an accepted pilgrimage, rewarded effort, and forgiven sin.
rows.anchor: بالفتح يحصل الحج ، ثم بالحج تحصل المغفرة ، ألا ترى إلى دعاء النبي عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may mean that the conquest makes the Prophet's forgiveness and protection from sin publicly known; after the Year of the Elephant, Mecca was expected to be conquered only by God's beloved, forgiven servant.
rows.anchor: المراد منه التعريف تقديره إنا فتحنا لك ليعرف أنك مغفور ، معصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer reads the sin as the sins of the believers.
rows.anchor: أحدها : المراد ذنب المؤمنين ثانيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer reads it as leaving what was better.
rows.anchor: ثانيها : المراد ترك الأفضل ثالثها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another answer means minor sins, which prophets may commit deliberately or through forgetfulness; this view says that such protection guards them from conceit.
rows.anchor: الصغائر فإنها جائزة على الأنبياء بالسهو والعمد ، وهو يصونهم عن العجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further answer takes the forgiveness to mean infallibility; Razi says he explained this in Sūrat al-Qitāl.
rows.anchor: رابعها : المراد العصمة / وقد بينا وجهه في سورة القتال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What came before and after” may promise that the Prophet will not sin after prophethood.
rows.anchor: أنه وعد النبي عليه السلام بأنه لا يذنب بعد النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean what came before the conquest and what came after it.
rows.anchor: ما تقدم على الفتح ، وما تأخر عن الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may be a generalizing expression: an impossible extension, such as striking people one will never meet, conveys comprehensiveness.
rows.anchor: العموم يقال اضرب من لقيت ومن لا تلقاه ، مع أن من لا يلقى لا يمكن ضربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may cover the periods before and after prophethood, with the former forgiven and the latter protected by infallibility.
rows.anchor: من قبل النبوة ومن بعدها ، وعلى هذا فما قبل النبوة بالعفو وما بعدها بالعصمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi rejects the claim that the earlier sin concerned Māriya and the later one Zaynab as the most far-fetched, incoherent reading.
rows.anchor: قول بعضهم : ما تقدم من أمر مارية ، وما تأخر من أمر زينب ، وهو أبعد الوجوه وأسقطها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completing the favor may mean that the obligations were completed at the conquest when pilgrimage became obligatory, since obligations are blessings.
rows.anchor: التكاليف عند الفتح تمت حيث وجب الحج ، وهو آخر التكاليف ، والتكاليف نعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean that God cleared the land of the Prophet's significant opponents: some had died at Badr and the rest believed or sought safety at the conquest.
rows.anchor: يتم نعمته عليك بإخلاء الأرض لك عن معانديك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favor may be God's answering the Prophet's request for conquest in this world and accepting his intercession for even very grave sins in the next.
rows.anchor: في الدنيا باستجابة دعائك في طلب الفتح ، وفي الآخرة بقول شفاعتك في الذنوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clearest reading of guidance is that God keeps the Prophet on the straight path until no misleader can sway him or compel disbelief; this accords with Islam being approved as the religion.
rows.anchor: أظهرها : يديمك على الصراط المستقيم حتى لا يبقى من يلتفت إلى قوله من المضلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conquest may lead to guidance by making believers more willing to fight through immediate gains and promised future reward; jihad is walking God's path.
rows.anchor: جعل الفتح سببا للهداية إلى / الصراط المستقيم ، لأنه سهل على المؤمنين الجهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause may disclose that the Prophet is on the straight path, since only someone on God's path could achieve such a conquest, as shown by the event of the Elephant.
rows.anchor: المراد التعريف ، أي ليعرف أنك على صراط مستقيم ، من حيث إن الفتح لا يكون إلا على يد من يكون على صراط الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conquest made God's victory visible and the Prophet's mission widely known.
rows.anchor: لأن بالفتح ظهر النصر واشتهر الأمر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains “mighty victory” as victory at a moment of might, analogous to describing a life as satisfied, meaning one that brings satisfaction.
rows.anchor: ما قاله الزمخشري أنه يحتمل وجوها ثلاثة الأول : معناه نصر إذ عز ، كقوله { فى عيشة راضية }

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also allows a figurative attribution: the victory is described with the quality of the person who wins, as in calling speech truthful for its speaker.
rows.anchor: وصف النصر بما يوصف به المنصور إسنادا مجازيا يقال له كلام صادق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: A third possibility from al-Zamakhshari is that it means a victory whose possessor is mighty.
rows.anchor: المراد نصرا عزيزا صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those paraphrases are needed only if ʿazīz means victorious; if it means precious, rare, or greatly needed, the phrase needs no such reinterpretation.
rows.anchor: إذا قلنا : العزيز هو النفيس القليل النظير ، أو المحتاج إليه القليل الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The victory was precious and unprecedented: taking God's House from entrenched unbelievers without an army.
rows.anchor: النصر كان محتاجا إليه ومثله لم يوجد وهو أخذ بيت الله من الكفار المتمكنين فيه من غير عدد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic normally names a subject with the first of several coordinated verbs and omits it afterward; repeating “God” with victory therefore teaches how victory is attained.
rows.anchor: الأفعال الكثيرة إذا صدرت من فاعل يظهر اسمه في الفعل الأول ، ولا يظهر فيما بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scripture repeatedly attributes victory to God, including the cited verses in al-Rūm, al-Anfāl, al-Naṣr, and al-Ṣaff.
rows.anchor: ولهذا قلما ذكر الله النصر من غير إضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Victory comes through patience, patience comes from God, and patience is a settled heart attained through remembering God.
rows.anchor: النصر بالصبر ، والصبر بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying “We opened” and then “that He may forgive you,” rather than “We opened to forgive you,” magnifies the conquest.
rows.anchor: قال : { إنا فتحنا } ثم قال : { ليغفر لك الله } ولم يقل إنا فتحنا لنغفر لك تعظيما لأمر الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness is a general divine benefit, since God forgives all sins and forgives lesser sins for whomever He wills.
rows.anchor: إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If forgiveness here means infallibility, that too is not unique to this Prophet, since other messengers were infallible.
rows.anchor: غيره من الرسل كان معصوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Completion of favor is shared with other communities, as God also completed the religion and blessed the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: قال الله تعالى : { اليوم أكملت لكم دينكم وأتممت عليكم نعمتى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance is also universal rather than exclusive to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وكذلك الهداية قال الله تعالى : { يهدى * إليه من يشاء } فعمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Victory is promised to all messengers, as stated in the cited verses from al-Ṣāffāt.
rows.anchor: إنهم لهم المنصورون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Unlike the other benefits, this opening was unique to the Prophet; “We” and “for you” honor it as a favor done for his sake.
rows.anchor: وأما الفتح فلم يكن لأحد غير النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ، فعظمه بقوله تعالى : { إنا فتحنا لك فتحا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here al-dīn means requital: the appointed gathering is the reckoning, and requital is punishment; the warning says reckoning and punishment will both be fully delivered.
rows.anchor: أي الجزاء كائن ، وعلى هذا فالإبعاد بالحشر في الموعد هو الحساب والجزاء هو العقاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing the message, the Messenger should begin by affirming God's oneness and preventing people from associating partners with Him.
rows.anchor: لما قرر الرسالة ذكر ما ينبغي أن يبتدىء به الرسول وهو التوحيد ومنع الخلق عن الإشراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question “Have you seen?” refutes the claim by directing attention to its obvious absurdity, like asking people to look at a weak man claiming kingship.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى إبطال قولهم بنفس القول كما أن ضعيفا إذا ادعى الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks how such idols could be associated with God, given what they are.
rows.anchor: أي كما هما فكيف تشركونهما بالله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine tāʾ in al-Lāt is like that in Manāt; it is written in its extended form so pausing does not make it resemble the name Allah, whose hāʾ is original.
rows.anchor: والتاء في اللات تاء تأنيث كما في المناة لكنها تكتب مطولة لئلا يوقف عليها فتصير هاء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari derives al-Lāt from lawā, “to turn around”: its original form was lawya, with the yāʾ dropped and the wāw changed to alif.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري هي فعله من لوى يلوي ، وذلك لأنهم كانوا يلوون عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading with doubled tāʾ derives al-Lāt from a man who mixed food with butter and fed people; an idol was made in his image, and on this account al-Lāt is masculine.
rows.anchor: قرىء اللات بالتشديد من لت ، قيل إنه مأخوذ من رجل كان يلت بالسمن الطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says al-ʿUzzā was a tree worshipped by the Arabs; Khālid b. al-Walīd cut it down, killed the exposed-haired demon that emerged, and returned to tell the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وأما العزى فتأنيث الأعز وهي شجرة كانت تعبد ، فبعث النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم خالد بن الوليد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: After Khālid reported what happened, the Prophet said that this was al-ʿUzzā and it would never be worshipped again.
rows.anchor: وأخبره بما رأى وفعل فقال تلك العزى ولن تعبد أبدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manāt was a rock idol associated with al-Ṣafā and was a stone belonging to Hudhayl and Khuzāʿa.
rows.anchor: وأما مناة فهي فعلة صنم الصفا ، وهي صخرة كانت لهذيل وخزاعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word “other” normally requires the first and second items to share a category, which makes “the third other” grammatically puzzling.
rows.anchor: الآخر لا يصح أن يقال إلا إذا كان الأول مشاركا للثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One answer treats “other” as a term of disparagement, as in 7:39, and ranks Manāt last: the human-shaped idol outranks the plant-shaped one, which outranks the stone one.
rows.anchor: الأخرى كما هي تستعمل للذم ، قال الله تعالى : { قالت * أولاهم لاخراهم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second answer supplies omitted words: the first two idols are falsely worshipped, while Manāt is the other idol worshipped.
rows.anchor: فيه محذوف تقديره { أفرءيتم اللات والعزى } المعبودين بالباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third answer says there were many idols, so any idol after al-Lāt and al-ʿUzzā could be called a third, and Manāt another one.
rows.anchor: الأصنام كان فيها كثرة واللات والعزى إذا أخذتا متقدمتين فكل صنمة توجد فهي ثالثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A fourth answer posits fronting and postponement: the phrase means “Manāt, the other, third.”
rows.anchor: فيه تقديم وتأخير تقديره ومناة الأخرى الثالثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The other” can also refer to someone assumed or understood though not previously mentioned, as in a person complaining that another nuisance has arrived.
rows.anchor: الأخرى تستعمل لموهوم أو مفهوم وإن لم يكن مشهورا ولا مذكورا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed fāʾ makes the challenge follow immediately from the preceding display of God's great signs: after hearing of their reach and power, compare them with the idols' insignificance.
rows.anchor: فقال بالفاء أي عقيب ما سمعتم من عظمة آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted completion is: if they truly saw these idols, they would know the idols cannot be God's partners; the brief question itself signals the claim's falsity, as with a weak pretender to kingship.
rows.anchor: فإن رأيتموها علمتم أنها لا تصلح شركاء ، نظيره ما ذكرنا فيمن ينكر كون ضعيف يدعي ملكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading says their feminine and divine labels are empty names: the idols are neither truly female nor deities.
rows.anchor: قيل معناه : إن هي إلا أسماء ، أي كونها إناثا وكونها معبودات أسماء لا مسمى لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading says they call an idol al-ʿUzzā though it has no might.
rows.anchor: وقيل أسماء أي قلتم بعضها عزى ولا عزة لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third reading says they call the idols gods even though they are not gods.
rows.anchor: وقيل قلتم إنها آلهة وليست بآلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's explanation answers their claim that angels are God's daughters: they reasoned that angels came directly from God without an intermediary, called them offspring, and inferred daughters from their feminine names.
rows.anchor: الملائكة أولاد الله بمعنى أنهم وجدوا بسببه من غير واسطة فقلنا إنهم أولاده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God rejects these self-invented labels because they imply deficiency; suggestive names may be used for God only when revelation supplies them, while people may not invent such names.
rows.anchor: هذه الأسماء استنبطتموها أنتم بهوى أنفسكم وأطلقتم على الله ما يوهم النقص وذلك غير جائز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun “they” most naturally refers to the names just mentioned: the idols' names are the labels the audience devised.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أنها عائدة إلى أمر معلوم وهو الأسماء كأنه قال ما هذه الأسماء التي وضعتموها أنتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to the idols themselves, hyperbolically reducing something without the relevant qualities to a mere name, as in 12:40.
rows.anchor: هي عائدة إلى الأصنام بأنفسها أي ما هذه الأصنام إلا أسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blame is completed by “God sent down no authority”: conventional names are acceptable only if their benefit does not carry greater harm, and implying deficiency in God is a greater harm than the benefit of these labels.
rows.anchor: ولا يتم الذم إلا بقوله تعالى : { ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is neither revealed nor rational authority for these names; a rational name must be free of outweighing harm.
rows.anchor: فلم يوجد في هذه الأسماء دليل نقلي ولا وجه عقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the names predated the audience, everyone who uses them acts like their originator; the first namer had no rational proof, so imitation cannot excuse those who follow him.
rows.anchor: كل من يطلق هذه الألفاظ فهو كالمبتدىء الواضع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “you named them” can linguistically mean “you placed names for them” or “you called them by these names.”
rows.anchor: التسمية وضع الاسم فكأنه قال أسماء وضعتموها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi's semantic answer is that “names you named” asserts names without real referents; “names you named by” would grant the idols an additional status beyond their names.
rows.anchor: إذا قال : { إن هى إلا أسماء سميتموها } أي وضعتموها في أنفسها لا مسميات لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison with Maryam does not refute this: that verse uses two objects, recognizing Maryam herself as well as her name, whereas this verse recognizes only names.
rows.anchor: هناك قال : { سميتها مريم } فذكر المفعولين فاعتبر حقيقة مريم بقوله { سميتها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in “with it no authority” has a comitative sense, as when one says that someone departed with his family and possessions.
rows.anchor: كما يستعمل القائل ارتحل فلان بأهله ومتاعه ، أي ارتحل ومعه الأهل والمتاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A recitation with tāʾ addresses the audience, matching “you and your fathers”; it may be an aside to the Prophet that they follow conjecture, so he should disregard them.
rows.anchor: قرىء { إن تتبعون } بالتاء على الخطاب ، وهو ظاهر مناسب لقوله تعالى : { أنتم وءاباؤكم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the tāʾ reading addresses someone else, perhaps the fathers: when they claimed to inherit the names, the reply says the fathers themselves named them and followed conjecture.
rows.anchor: المراد آباءهم وتقديره هو أنه لما قال : { سميتموها أنتم } كأنهم قالوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present tense may project a time after the speech, as in the description of the Cave sleepers' dog in 18:18.
rows.anchor: وبصيغة المستقبل أيضا كأنه يفرض الزمان بعد زمان الكلام كما في قوله تعالى : { وكلبهم باسط ذراعيه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further possible subject is disbelievers generally: they follow only conjecture.
rows.anchor: أن يكون المراد عامة الكفار كأنه قال : إن يتبع الكافرون إلا الظن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Conjecture contrasts with knowledge, though either term can be used figuratively for the other; zann itself implies obscurity, as in a well of uncertain water or a person suspected without certainty.
rows.anchor: أما الظن فهو خلاف العلم وقد استعمل مجازا مكان العلم والعلم مكانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Razi cites the divine saying, “I am as My servant thinks of Me,” as an apparent counterexample to condemning conjecture.
rows.anchor: أنا عند ظن عبدي بي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One may act on a preponderant probability when certainty is inaccessible; these idolaters are blameworthy because revealed guidance made certainty available to them.
rows.anchor: يجوز بناء الأمر على الظن الغالب عند العجز عن درك اليقين
